steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: *gasp* —!
Over here!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Hurry! Grab my hand!
A single, solitary boat.
How far is it from the Eye of Iberia? How far is it from Gran Faro?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Ah, um, okay—!
Irene grabs onto his hand.
There is no difference between the hand of an Ægir and that of a Liberi.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um— S-Sorry, I'm not very strong...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: It's... fine...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I was scared out of my wits when I saw the ship explode in the distance! Are you all okay?!

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: As long as you're fine, Irene. Adjust your breathing. You know how to swim, right?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Luckily for us, the waters are pretty calm right now.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: *gasp*... *gasp*... Where are the others?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...I need to check on a few things.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Just now, was that... Ægir? This close to us? Has the Stultifera been circling above an Ægir city this entire time?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: We might've been able to find a way in to check out the city on our own, but you never would've made it.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Plus, the squad captain didn't seem keen on just going home happily ever after. And no way would there be a city this close to land; I don't remember anything like that.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... *pant*...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: So, are you going to head back to that city?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No. Gladiia said this place is also Seaborn territory. The city must be a refugee village.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The Ægir you people call Islanders are refugees from the collapse of the cities closest to land.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: ...We should go help them.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Two things.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Ulpianus isn't dead, but he refused to work with us.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: And there are still other Seaborn nearby, drawn here by that spurt of evolution. The entire swarm is extremely restless.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We can use this opportunity to get back down there, but we wouldn't be able to leave.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: So... we finally found a city from our homeland, and now we're just going to turn around and leave?
Gladiia wordlessly glances at Skadi.
She hides it well. Just as she did herself, in all those silent moments when she gently rubbed her neck.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We don't have a choice.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Why?!

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: There shouldn't be a city here.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: We... We should head back to shore and regroup.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Our duty is to defend Ægir, not to 'go home.'

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: How'd you manage this?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Huh? Oh, are you talking to me? What do you mean?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: This ship is even more bare-bones than ours was. And how did you find us? The sea is incredibly vast.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I compared each of the signals from the Stultifera Navis to her location... and discovered a pattern. So I thought, um, it might be worth a shot...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Worth a shot? What kind of deviation was there in that pattern?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Umm, two to three hundred nautical miles?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: That can't even be called a pattern. If you had bet wrong, you would've had slim to no chance of meeting up with us, and died out at sea on your own.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...You're a lunatic.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: But... I wanted to ask a question... So please don't laugh at me, ma'am.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I can't laugh anymore.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Am I a great person?

steps.name: Thiago
steps.text: Your grandparents, your parents... two generations of Gran Faro gave everything they had for this blueprint. Their greatness should have been immortalized forever.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I wouldn't go that far.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Maybe a lucky one.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Haha... Is that so?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Maestro... and my other colleagues in the Inquisition, always held this belief:

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Only those who've sacrificed themselves are worthy of the word, 'great.' In every moment where we're fighting for Iberia and struggling to survive, we are nothing more than ordinary people, striding forward with enormous responsibilities.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: And it's not that Inquisitors enjoy belittling ourselves. We've simply chosen to deal with Iberia in the harshest way possible because the moment we let our guards down, we will be undone.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But until then, as long as the will of man is enough to ignite this lantern, then I believe... there isn't any difference between us.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: We're just like all those citizens struggling bitterly in their own ways. As long as we have goodwill to spare, they too are soldiers willing to lay down their lives for the restoration of their homeland.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Just like the laborers of old Gran Faro.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Jordi, luck won't be on your side forever. If you have a chance to contact the Inquisition again... Um, what I mean is, if you want to work with us—

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —You'll definitely have that opportunity.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Haha... Well, I actually... Um, just out of curiosity...

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I see you've brought back some of the Stultifera's timeless knowledge. Might you actually be—

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You managed to rescue three Hunters in a single breath. As an Ægir, your actions might be worth a medal from the consul herself.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Swimming back would've been very hard. And who knows what could happen right above their nest?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I have no idea what compelled someone like you, born in Gran Faro, to go this far, but good job.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: On behalf of the Ægir... and the Iberians.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: ...Mhm.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Then let's head back home!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Welcome back, Hunters. And Irene, of course.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: The High Inquisitor, he...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: How did you know?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: We've already sorted through his relics. Including those of our comrades who died beneath this lighthouse.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: We won't be able to deal with them properly until the Penal Battalion arrives though.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: These lowly Sea Terrors could not defeat High Inquisitor Dario, but in order to protect the Eye of Iberia, he chose to lay down his life to buy time.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Inquisitors have no time to grieve, Irene. Dario had great expectations for you, and you must move forward.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Yes, sir!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: However...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: His lantern remains intact, and I've placed it over there.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Go now.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Yes, sir...

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Seems like the Penal Battalion ran into some trouble. So much for the great naval power of Iberia.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: ...So the Stultifera Navis has sunk. This isn't quite the outcome we were expecting either.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Indeed. Even for us, this is a significant setback.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: But we learned quite a few things, and—

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You found an Ægir city.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Kal'tsit has already shared her conjecture with me, so perhaps you will wish to hear it too.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The Inquisition has always believed in maintaining control. From Sal Viento to the Stultifera, we will gradually recapture the glory that rightfully belongs to Iberia.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But we are forced to admit that, perhaps, even preserving the status quo is enough to... stretch our forces thin.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Madame Consul—

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: What did you witness aboard that ship?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: This is his lantern... The High Inquisitor's lantern... Scorched black, thick with the stench of Sea Terrors.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I... High Inquisitor...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Maestro!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I completed the Inquisition's mission! I found the Stultifera!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Unfortunately, it ended up sinking! But... aboard the ship, every single Iberian! In their own way, they were fighting until the very end!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: High Inquisitor!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I now... understand the significance of passing judgment! I understand the enemy we face!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I— will not hesitate, nor will I falter!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: For Iberia's prosperity, for Iberia's defense, and for Iberia's orderliness and integrity, I shall raise my sword and my light!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Alfonso, he... No, this can't be!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Sixty years? What torture is this? Even a criminal subjected to the harshest of punishment would not last for a year!

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But he... he...
Carmen falls silent. He leans over and sits down on the reef.

Sea Terrors carcasses are piled high into a mountain. There is no trace of the eldritch beasts, only the remaining tendrils of the nethersea brand retreating back to sea. The ocean's surface emits a pale blue light, usurping the sky's privilege.
He should be enjoying this victory. He accomplished what the Inquisition set out to do. The Penal Battalion is about to arrive, and all things are about to reach a satisfactory conclusion.
But he can only remain silent.
Up until a steam whistle roars in the distance. The Penal Battalion has arrived at the Eye of Iberia.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You can see the corner of the town from here. If I remember right, it was called... Reconstruction Hill.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Thiago didn't pass peacefully, and I don't know if that's a good or a bad thing. But...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Still, thank you all.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Don't mention it.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: I don't mind dedicating a song to a hero at a solemn funeral.

steps.name: Alty
steps.text: Seems like Frost is back.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Mhm. We'll head back too in a little bit.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: What about you, Iberian? You've had a rough few days, haven't you?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Gran Faro is Thiago's hometown. Just as Ægir is home to all of you, as well as my Abyssal Hunter buddies.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Maybe I joke around too much normally, and forgot...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That Iberia is also my home. To be honest, this isn't cathartic at all.

steps.name: Aya
steps.text: Wasn't that doctor going to help you out with something? You've been working for her, haven't you?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: No, that's already dealt with. That's why I'm willing to stay with Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: That said...

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: ...I didn't do a damn thing.

steps.name: Tense Townsperson
steps.text: Hurry, hurry! Move the supplies into the warehouse!

steps.name: Tense Townsperson
steps.text: Huh, what about the number of tents? Didn't the old guy already explain it?! Ugh—

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Tense Townsperson
steps.text: J-Jordi? You're back?

steps.name: Tense Townsperson
steps.text: What? The Inquisition took you away and actually let you come back? Where did you go?

steps.name: Tense Townsperson
steps.text: A bunch of people from the Penal Battalion took us away, but then brought us back into town. Seems like they're going to war with something, and now they want us setting up tents.

steps.name: Tense Townsperson
steps.text: Jeez, what's going to happen to Gran Faro? Oh, and uh, have you seen Thiago?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Jordi Fontanarossa.

steps.name: Tense Townsperson
steps.text: Ah... Lord Carmen, sir... And Madame Inquisitor!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Mhm.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: We'd like to have a private chat with this Ægir.

steps.name: Tense Townsperson
steps.text: Ah, of course! Right away!

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: M-Me?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Come with me. Let's take a walk around town, shall we?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Irene made up her mind on the way back.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: M-Made up her mind? About what?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Originally, High Inquisitor Dario intended to entrust Irene to me, so that I could cultivate her until she was prepared for the seat of High Inquisitor.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: His death in battle was unexpected. Though the day would've come sooner or later, he did not have to accept his fate so soon.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: But Irene has made up her mind.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: She will give up her position as Inquisitor.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Huh? Wait, what? Why?!

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: This is a decision I've come to after a lot of thought.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: It has nothing to do with you, though, so please just keep listening.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Oh, okay...

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: The problem is you, Ægir. You know too much. You're too deeply involved. And the Ægir in this town are too blasphemous.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: You've also been of great help.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: As frail and weak as you are, your death would've been but another grain of sand. But you have shown great strength. Even if it's nothing more than your own little spark, it is still valuable.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I keep thinking... Why am I still alive? I'm not as noble as you any of you, or as resolute.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Jordi, you will be... the first Ægir to join the Inquisition.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Huh? Wha–? Me? Join the Inquisition?

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: Strictly speaking, I won't give you a chance to refuse. Gran Faro needs more hands than ever, and you will play a pivotal role as an Ægir.

steps.name: Saint Carmen
steps.text: After that, hrmm. Maybe I could use a young secretary?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Wait, hold on, you want me? To join the Inquisition?

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: B-But I'm not sure if I want—

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I know you don't. Many members of the Inquisition hold deeply-rooted prejudices against the Ægir, and wouldn't want you joining either.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: But don't you want to see it? The future that Iberia once promised to Gran Faro, and to Thiago?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Joining the Inquisition will be a test. As an Ægir, you wouldn't be wrong to treat it as a trial by fire. Or as practice for enduring hardship.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Don't get the wrong idea.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I... I'll give it some thought.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: Then, what about you, Doña Irene? Your maestro...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: My status as an Inquisitor hasn't done me any favors in my relationship with the Abyssal Hunters, or even the Ægir, so I got rid of it.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: But abandoning a faith that's supported me to this day, especially after the untimely demise of my maestro... has not been an easy decision.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Please... let's not talk about this now. Maybe if we meet again someday.

steps.name: Jordi
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: It's just...
Irene looks at the sculpture in the plaza. A scaled-down version of the Eye of Iberia.
In the chaos of battle, streets were torn up, houses were destroyed, and makeshift tents were erected.
And the statue has always looked out over all of it.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Even though our enemy is well beyond the reach of the law, Iberia must banish this blasphemy.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Victory will be ours.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I owe you my gratitude, Frost. You helped Jordi, as well as the Hunters.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Say no more, it was just a little workout. Those disobedient little rascals aren't the only ones who can change the direction of the tides.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Next time, make sure you come cheer for us though.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Alrighty, I'm gonna go catch up with Aya and the others then.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Stepped out a second and they went and ghosted me.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs with slight dissatisfaction)

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Oh right, Kal'tsit...

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Since we came all this way, we can't just go back empty-handed. We can awaken whenever you're ready.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: Aya would say the same.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Thank you very much. Maybe, in time, we really will be able to form a working partnership.

steps.name: Frost
steps.text: (Riffs to signify her departure)

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: So, this is the truth that Breogan discovered.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: 'Feranmut' and 'Leviathan'. The connection between the two.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: If these massive creatures had disappeared from the ocean long ago, yet continued to survive on land in this form—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: They're not the same, Gladiia.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Great Yan, Sargon, Sami. These places have all faced grave situations caused by Feranmuts.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But remember.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The ocean as a catalyst of mutation is both unique and irreplaceable. Even I cannot comprehend its principles, or its trajectory.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: All I can see are the results, and make deductions from that. And what I predict is a terrible, terrible future.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Also, I'd imagine Breogan discovered more than one truth. And as you said, if there is another Abyssal Hunter still alive—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: There is more than one Leviathan. The one we slew is but a small part of what the Ægir civilization concealed.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Besides...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The one you killed still lives on inside Skadi's body.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Then my worst-case scenario came true. You made the right choice not to return to Ægir.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Rhodes Island has already done enough for us. You have your own work ahead of you. As for what comes next, we will take that step ourselves.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Rhodes Island... has its responsibilities. Our most stellar operators will ensure that the organization continues running.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But I have my own responsibilities, across all these countless years.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Time and again, I have tried to resolve the problem facing Ægir. But it is far removed from the land, unique and without precedent.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We can't wait any longer.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The ocean's problem is of the same scale as Originium.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If civilization is to continue, then we must overcome this calamity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Even as this world faces constant threats, divisions grow and wars ignite without cease, just as the name Stultifera Navis implies.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Terra is certainly full of fools, both malicious and ignorant, but it is also full of saints, who seek reason above madness and chaos.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now that you know the source of evolution, all our conjectures have been verified. Ægir's cities are within reach, and even arrogant Iberia has emerged from its shell.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Chief Designer of Warfare, let us begin.

steps.name: Rocinante
steps.text: (Shakes neck around in dissatisfaction)

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Calm down, Rocinante.

steps.name: Rocinante
steps.text: (Swings neck around more violently)

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Rocinante...

steps.name: Rocinante
steps.text: (Brays)

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...Where are we going?

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: The terrible waves, are coming.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: We, will defeat them.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: We, are the terrible waves.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The terrible waves. As long as there is water in the ocean, a moon in the heavens, and wind in the sky, the waves will not abate.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The enemy you see in your madness is truly too majestic.

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Go! (Rasping growl) Hyah!

steps.name: Rocinante
steps.text: (Elated braying)

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: (Rasping roar) —!

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: I will not allow, the sea, another ripple!

steps.name: The Last Knight
steps.text: Go!
